readings.title: The meter before opening time
readings.instruction: Read the original simulation passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: Brook Water Centre asked a café to record its meter when closing and before opening the next morning. The readings increased even on nights when no cleaning was scheduled. A plumber found a leaking pipe behind a cupboard. Repairing it reduced water use without asking staff to wash fewer dishes. The café still worked on careful habits, but the investigation changed the order of its efforts. What appeared to be a problem of daily behaviour partly came from hidden equipment failure. Measuring at a quiet time helped separate the two.
knowledgePoints: 阅读：主旨、细节、推断与语境词义

options.D: They showed water use when no planned activity should require it.

questions.explanation: 文中明确支持 They showed water use when no planned activity should require it.；其余选项与所述措施、原因或事实不符。

readings.title: Signs beside the sink
readings.instruction: Read the original simulation passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: A college placed 'Save Water' posters around its kitchens. Students agreed with the message but were unsure what action was expected. A catering assistant added a specific instruction beside the vegetable sink: rinse produce in a bowl rather than under a running tap. Staff demonstrated the method while maintaining the kitchen's cleaning requirements. The new sign connected a general aim with a task people performed every day. It did not ask them to use too little water for hygiene. Useful advice had to show where savings were appropriate and where proper cleaning remained essential.

readings.title: A lawn in a dry month
readings.instruction: Read the original simulation passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: During a dry spell, a housing committee debated whether to water its entire lawn every evening. A gardener explained that newly planted trees needed attention more urgently than established grass. The committee prioritised those trees, checked restrictions and watered at a suitable time. Parts of the lawn turned brown, causing some complaints. A notice explained the choice and showed signs that the grass was still alive. The grounds did not look perfect, but limited water was directed where it could prevent lasting damage. The decision balanced appearance with longer-term needs.
knowledgePoints: 阅读：主旨、细节、推断与语境词义

readings.title: Comparing two shower heads
readings.instruction: Read the original simulation passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: A sports centre replaced several shower heads with lower-flow models. Managers compared the next month's total water use with the previous month and announced a large saving. An employee noted that the centre had also closed for a week of floor repairs. The team recalculated use per visitor and continued measuring after normal opening resumed. The devices still appeared useful, but the estimated saving was smaller. Correcting the claim did not mean the project had failed. It made the result more credible and helped managers decide whether further replacements were worth the cost.
knowledgePoints: 阅读：主旨、细节、推断与语境词义

translation.stem:
Translate the following original passage into Chinese. Preserve the meaning and logical relationships.

A small leak may seem unimportant because each drop is tiny. Over time, however, the total amount of wasted water can be considerable. Measuring use helps people identify where a change is needed. Lasting savings usually combine careful habits with well-maintained equipment.
translation.referenceAnswer: 小漏水看起来也许无关紧要，因为每滴水都很少。然而，时间一长，浪费的水量就可能相当可观。计量用水有助于人们发现哪些地方需要改进。持久的节水效果通常需要良好习惯与维护得当的设备相结合。
translation.explanation: 参考译文仅示范一种表达。评分时关注信息完整性、转折和条件等逻辑关系；意思准确且中文自然的其他译法同样有效。

writing.stem:
Write an English response of about 120 words to the following original simulation task. Use your own examples and organise your ideas clearly.

Explain how a college could reduce unnecessary water use. Propose one change in behaviour and one improvement to facilities.
writing.sampleAnswer: Our college could reduce unnecessary water use through one practical habit and one improvement to facilities. In teaching kitchens, vegetables could be rinsed in suitable bowls instead of under continuously running taps, while proper hygiene requirements remain essential. Staff should demonstrate the method rather than rely on a general poster. The college should also check meters at quiet times to identify possible leaks and repair faulty equipment promptly. Monthly totals should be compared with the number of users, because a holiday closure can make savings look larger than they are. These actions would combine responsible behaviour with reliable facilities. Students are more likely to support conservation when advice is specific and the college maintains its own equipment properly.
